Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks · Household, washing & chores

wash verb

also wash hands, wash your hands, wash the face, wash your face, wash yourself, have a wash, get washed, wash (oneself)

classical

Traupman 404

lavō, lavāre, lāvī, lavātum

verb, first conjugation

Other ancient forms include the infinitive lavere and participles lautus and lōtus.

Other words

  • lavārī (sē lavāre) — wash (oneself), bathe

    the passive of lavō used as a middle, or the reflexive · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.129: cum socerīs generī nōn lavantur (Lewis & Short s.v. lavō); Caes. BG 4.1: lavantur in flūminibus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 39: wash, intr., lavārī, sē lavāre; Traupman 404

    English “wash” without an object is the passive in Latin: lavor, I wash (myself), I have a bath; the imperative to a child is Tē lavā (Traupman 36).

Examples

  • Pōma lavā.

    Wash the fruit.composed

  • Prīmum manūs lavēmus.

    First, let’s wash our hands.composed

  • Tū pōma lavā; ego secābō.

    You wash the fruit; I’ll do the cutting.composed

  • Lavā tibi manūs.

    Wash your hands.composed

  • Manūs lavēmus.

    Let’s wash our hands.composed

  • Faciem lavā.

    Wash your face.composed

  • Aqua calida est.

    The water is warm.composed

  • Agedum, tē lavā et dentēs pūrgā.

    Come on, wash and brush your teeth.Traupman 36

See also rinse, dry, hand, face, soap, bath.
